digest.headline: US tech stocks rebounded as gold prices eased following domestic inflation data.

lede.b: The Nasdaq 100 index recovered after previously dipping into bear market territory, which means a drop of 20% or more from recent highs. Investor Michael Burry exited a broad short position, which is a bet that prices will fall, and set up a temporary long position, which is a bet that prices will rise. Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq futures edged higher after a volatile trading session. Gold prices eased as domestic inflation data reinforced market expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes. The incoming economic figures prompted traders to reprice monetary policy tightening paths.
lede.i: The Nasdaq 100 index recovered after dipping into bear market territory, while semiconductor shares lagged. Investor Michael Burry exited a broad short position on the Nasdaq and established a temporary long position. Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq futures edged higher after a volatile trading session. Gold prices eased as domestic inflation data reinforced market expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes. The incoming economic figures prompted traders to reprice monetary policy tightening paths.
lede.a: The Nasdaq 100 index retraced its descent into bear market territory despite lagging semiconductor performance. Investor Michael Burry liquidated a broad short exposure on the Nasdaq in favour of a temporary long duration. Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq futures edged higher following a volatile trading session. Gold prices eased as domestic inflation data reinforced market expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes. The incoming economic figures prompted traders to reprice monetary policy tightening paths.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: US tech stocks rebound, futures rise, and gold drops

stories.t: Tech Stocks Rebound After Sharp Selloff
stories.b: The Nasdaq 100 index, which tracks one hundred large technology companies, fell into a bear market before bouncing back. Chips lagged behind other sectors during the session. Investor Michael Burry closed his broad Nasdaq short position and switched to a temporary long position.
stories.i: The Nasdaq 100 index dipped into bear market territory before staging a recovery as semiconductor shares lagged. Investor Michael Burry exited a broad short position on the Nasdaq and established a temporary long position.
stories.a: The Nasdaq 100 breached bear market thresholds intraday prior to a mean-reverting bounce, weighed down by persistent underperformance in semiconductor equities. Michael Burry liquidated his extensive downside directional exposure against the Nasdaq, rotating into a transient long configuration.

stories.t: Futures Rise Following Market Volatility
stories.b: Stock futures for the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq rose following a wild market ride. Companies like Disney, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Deere, and Charter Communications drew investor focus. Asian stocks also rose as buyers stepped in to stabilize the artificial intelligence trade.
stories.i: Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq futures edged higher after a volatile trading session. Market participants focused on equities including Disney, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Deere, and Charter Communications. Asian equities advanced as dip buyers acted to stabilize the artificial intelligence trade.
stories.a: Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq futures printed modest gains following severe cross-asset turbulence. Micro-level price action concentrated on Disney, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Deere, and Charter Communications. Concurrently, regional Asian benchmarks appreciated as systematic dip-buying absorbed selling pressure in artificial intelligence proxies.

stories.t: Gold Eases on Inflation Data
stories.b: Gold prices eased after new American price data came out. The inflation figures reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve, which is the central bank of the United States that manages interest rates, will hike interest rates.
stories.i: Gold prices eased as domestic inflation data reinforced market expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes. The incoming economic figures prompted traders to reprice monetary policy tightening paths.
stories.a: Spot gold retraced as US inflation prints validated hawkish Federal Reserve rate-hike probabilities. Real yields adjusted higher as rate-market pricing priced out imminent easing trajectories.

politics.b: No political statements or policy updates were issued in the market reports.
politics.i: No political updates or governmental policy measures appeared in the session data.
politics.a: No sovereign political developments or administration policy shifts were registered in the reporting sources.

timeline: Michael Burry exited his Nasdaq short position.
Gold eased following US inflation data releases.
Nasdaq 100 rebounded after dipping into a bear market.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: UK inflation rises on energy costs

stories.t: Energy Costs Push Up Price Growth
stories.b: The rate at which prices go up across the economy is called inflation. This measures how much more everyday goods cost compared to before. Energy costs increased recently. These rising energy costs kept pressure on the Bank of England. That bank decides the cost of borrowing money.
stories.i: UK inflation increased over the reporting period. Energy costs drove the upward movement. Higher energy expenses maintained pressure on the Bank of England. Policymakers watch these metrics when setting monetary policy.
stories.a: Headline inflation printed higher as energy costs exerted upward pressure on the consumer price basket. The dynamic complicates the policy calculus for the Bank of England. Sticky energy components maintain the transmission channel of input costs into broader services.

politics.b: The government faces questions about the cost of living. Energy prices affect household bills across the country. Ministers monitor the economic data closely. Officials discuss potential responses to price increases.
politics.i: Elected officials face scrutiny over household energy bills. Ministers monitor macroeconomic data releases. Policy debates center on living costs and price stability.
politics.a: Lawmakers confront parliamentary scrutiny over household energy burdens. Fiscal authorities assess macroeconomic indicators for policy alignment. Cabinet members monitor price dynamics as living cost pressures persist.

timeline: Data shows UK inflation rising as energy costs keep pressure on the Bank of England.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German shares decline as economic growth eases

stories.t: Frankfurt equities drop
stories.b: German stocks fell at the end of the trading day. The DAX index dropped by 1.14%. Share prices moved lower as investors sold artificial intelligence stocks.
stories.i: German shares closed lower as the DAX fell 1.14%. A broad flight from artificial intelligence stocks drove the decline in Frankfurt.
stories.a: The DAX declined by 1.14% at the Frankfurt close. Broad sectoral liquidation in artificial intelligence equities drove the index lower.

stories.t: Economic growth slows
stories.b: German quarterly economic growth slowed down. This indicator measures the total value of goods and services produced. The DAX index declined alongside this easing growth.
stories.i: German quarterly GDP growth eased. The DAX index declined as this economic indicator cooled.
stories.a: German quarterly GDP growth eased alongside the contraction in the DAX index. Macroeconomic output deceleration accompanied the equity sell-off.

politics.a: No political updates were reported in the sources today.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Mitsui asset overhaul, crude shipments, and currency shifts

stories.t: Mitsui Plans Asset Overhaul
stories.b: Mitsui wants to change how its business works. The firm announced a plan worth $125bn to overhaul assets. The goal is to boost its return on equity. Return on equity is a measure of how well a company uses investments to grow profits.
stories.i: Mitsui targets a business asset overhaul valued at $125bn. The Japanese conglomerate implements this restructuring strategy to boost its return on equity. Management structures the portfolio realignment to improve capital efficiency across core divisions.
stories.a: Mitsui initiates a $125bn asset overhaul focused on return on equity expansion. The reallocation targets sub-performing units to compress capital intensity. Market participants must assess whether asset disposals dilute earnings power before realizing valuation multiples.

stories.t: Petrobras Crude Reaches Japan
stories.b: Petrobras shipped pre-salt crude to Japan for the first time. The tanker carried about 950,000 barrels from the Libra field to Idemitsu. The shipment happened because the Hormuz crisis cut Middle Eastern oil supplies.
stories.i: Petrobras completed its first shipment of pre-salt crude to Japan. The energy firm delivered roughly 950,000 barrels from the Libra field to Idemitsu. This diversion stems from Middle Eastern oil supply cuts driven by the Hormuz crisis.
stories.a: Petrobras executed a debut pre-salt crude delivery to Japan, dispatching approximately 950,000 barrels from the Libra field to Idemitsu. The transaction reflects trade flow realignments triggered by Middle Eastern supply disruptions under the Hormuz crisis.

stories.t: Currency Moves and Rice Ball Prices
stories.src: Euronext Markets · Seoul Economic Daily · WSJ
stories.b: The yen gained strength as the dollar slipped during an AI-driven market session. At the same time, convenience store rice balls in Japan neared 200 yen after an 80% jump. Bank of Japan Governor Ueda also stated he watches Federal Reserve moves closely.
stories.i: The yen rose alongside the Swiss franc as the dollar weakened in a volatile AI-driven session. Convenience store rice balls in Japan approached 200 yen following an 80% price jump. Bank of Japan Governor Ueda vowed to keep a careful eye on Federal Reserve decisions.
stories.a: The yen and the Swiss franc appreciated as the dollar retreated during volatile AI-driven trading sessions. Japanese convenience store rice balls traded near 200 yen following an 80% price surge. Bank of Japan Governor Ueda articulated continued scrutiny of Federal Reserve policy trajectories.

politics.b: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda stated he keeps a careful eye on the moves made by the Federal Reserve in the United States.
politics.i: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda vowed to monitor Federal Reserve policy developments.
politics.a: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda underscored attentiveness to Federal Reserve policy shifts.

timeline: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda vows to watch Federal Reserve moves.
Mitsui announces a $125bn asset overhaul plan.
Petrobras delivers its first pre-salt crude cargo to Japan.

China.label: China
China.sub: China Vanke debt talks, institutional fund buying, and Li Auto earnings

stories.t: China Vanke Seeks Further Debt Delay
stories.b: China Vanke is a big property developer in China that builds homes and commercial buildings. A bond is a certificate where a company borrows money from investors and promises to pay it back later with interest. China Vanke wants to push back the repayment date on a yuan-denominated bond coming due next month. This delay request shows ongoing financial stress in China's property construction sector. China Vanke asked for another extension on its debt obligations.
stories.i: China Vanke is seeking debt relief from investors for a maturing bond due next month. The developer is attempting to defer repayment as distress across the Chinese real estate sector deepens. Poly Developments and Holdings plans to issue 20 billion yuan in corporate bonds alongside these ongoing developer struggles. China Vanke is pursuing a maturity extension for the second time.
stories.a: China Vanke is attempting to negotiate another maturity extension on a forthcoming yuan bond, highlighting persistent solvency pressures within the domestic property sector. The builder's distress contrasts with primary market issuance plans, such as Poly Developments and Holdings moving to raise 20 billion yuan via corporate notes. Creditor willingness to accept further restructuring terms will dictate whether secondary yield spreads widen across the broader real estate credit curve.

stories.t: Institutions Launch Share Purchase Wave
stories.b: Institutions are large professional organizations like banks and investment funds that manage lots of money. A-shares are stocks of Chinese companies traded on domestic exchanges that local investors usually buy. Twenty-one financial institutions injected 2.7 billion yuan into buying these local shares to support the market. Ningquan Asset reopened its funds to new investors after taking a 13-month break. This institutional buying wave swept across the domestic exchange.
stories.i: Institutional investors injected 2.7 billion yuan to increase their A-share equity positions across the market. Twenty-one separate institutions participated in this self-purchase wave to boost domestic equities. Private manager Ningquan Asset simultaneously lifted its 13-month hiatus to reopen subscriptions to new investors. This coordinated deployment signals fresh capital allocation into onshore Chinese shares.
stories.a: A cohort of 21 institutional asset managers deployed a combined 2.7 billion yuan to increase onshore A-share exposure through proprietary fund purchases. This self-purchase wave coincides with Ningquan Asset lifting its 13-month closure to resume accepting allocations from new external investors. The net inflow reflects a tactical effort by domestic funds to signal conviction and absorb local equity supply.

stories.t: Li Auto Narrows Quarterly Loss
stories.b: Li Auto is a company that manufactures electric vehicles and sells them to drivers. Q3 refers to the third quarter, which is the three-month financial reporting period ending in September. Li Auto reported that its financial loss shrank significantly compared to earlier periods. Vehicle deliveries rose back up, though overall corporate profits have not returned yet. The company released its third-quarter earnings report detailing these metrics.
stories.i: Li Auto narrowed its net loss sharply during the third quarter as vehicle deliveries recovered. The electric vehicle maker released financial results showing delivery volumes rebounding after previous slumps. Bottom-line profitability remains elusive despite the higher delivery volume. The third-quarter earnings report details the gap between top-line unit sales and net earnings.
stories.a: Li Auto posted a sharply narrowed net loss for the third quarter driven by a sequential recovery in vehicle deliveries. The top-line volume rebound failed to translate into full net profitability, underscoring ongoing margin pressures within the competitive electric vehicle segment. The earnings figures illustrate that volume recovery is outpacing earnings normalization for the manufacturer.

politics.b: Chinese financial regulators monitor property developer debt restructurings and corporate bond issuance plans closely. Government authorities track domestic equity market stability as institutions deploy billions into local shares. Economic officials manage currency exchange rates as the yuan trades against the US dollar.
politics.i: Chinese regulatory bodies oversee corporate debt extensions and large-scale bond offerings from major developers like Poly Developments. Monetary authorities observe onshore equity interventions by institutional investors attempting to stabilize A-shares. The central bank manages foreign exchange dynamics as the yuan adjusts against the US dollar.
politics.a: State regulators oversee the systemic implications of sequential property developer debt defaults and large corporate refinancing programs. Monetary authorities monitor domestic equity stabilization efforts by institutional funds amidst fluctuating currency valuations against the US dollar. Macroeconomic policy levers remain focused on containing real estate credit contagion while supporting onshore capital formation.

timeline: China Vanke seeks an extension on a yuan bond due next month
Twenty-one institutions inject 2.7 billion yuan into A-share positions
Li Auto reports its third-quarter financial results with a narrowed loss

India.label: India
India.sub: IT stocks lead stock gains as currency falls

stories.t: Information Technology Shares Push Indexes Upward
stories.b: The stock market went up at first on November 26, 2026. This means the total value of companies went higher. Technology shares grew by 2%. The Nifty index reached nearly 25,850.
stories.i: Stock markets rose in early trade on November 26, 2026. Information technology shares gained 2%, pushing benchmarks higher. The Sensex climbed nearly 400 points from its lowest point.
stories.a: Equities advanced in early trade on November 26, 2026, underpinned by sustained foreign institutional investor inflows and an outperformance in the technology sector. The Sensex recovered nearly 400 points from session lows, while the Nifty hovered near 25,850.

stories.t: Rupee Declines Against the Dollar
stories.src: Rediff MoneyWiz · Reserve Bank of India
stories.b: The local currency dropped by 20 paise to 92.40 on November 26, 2026. This happened because of new taxes from America and expensive oil. Money changing hands in the overnight market showed an average rate of 5.72%.
stories.i: The rupee fell 20 paise to 92.40 on November 26, 2026, driven by new United States tariffs and high crude oil prices. Reserve Bank of India data showed overnight money market operations recorded a weighted average rate of 5.72% on November 25, 2026.
stories.a: The rupee depreciated by 20 paise to 92.40 on November 26, 2026, weighed down by renewed United States tariff threats and elevated crude prices. Meanwhile, Reserve Bank of India money market data for November 25, 2026, indicated that overnight volumes reached 7,79,137.97 crore rupees with a weighted average rate of 5.72%.

politics.b: Government officials faced pressure on currency values due to foreign taxes announced on November 26, 2026.
politics.i: Trade policy pressures from the United States affected currency valuations on November 26, 2026.
politics.a: External trade friction involving United States tariff announcements exerted downward pressure on the foreign exchange value on November 26, 2026.

timeline: Reserve Bank of India recorded total overnight money market operations volume at 7,79,137.97 crore rupees.
Stock indexes opened higher with IT shares gaining 2%, while the rupee fell 20 paise to 92.40.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras launches giant investment plan and payouts

stories.t: Petrobras reveals huge spending plan and extraordinary payout
stories.src: CPG Click Oil and Gas · The Globe and Mail · Inspenet
stories.b: Petrobras is a big energy company owned mostly by the state. It just launched a plan to spend $122 billion through 2031, which is an 11.9% increase in investment. The firm also approved an extraordinary payout of R$15.60 billion to its backers. At the same time, management says it has no new public hiring process planned after bringing on 6,000 workers since 2023.
stories.i: Petrobras unveiled an 11.9% increase in its business plan, targeting $122 billion in investments through 2031. The board approved an extraordinary remuneration of R$15.60 billion. Leadership confirmed that no new public hiring process is planned after the integration of 6,000 employees since 2023.
stories.a: Petrobras scaled its capital expenditure trajectory by 11.9% within a $122 billion framework extending to 2031. Concurrently, the entity sanctioned an extraordinary remuneration of R$15.60 billion. Headcount expansion remains frozen following the absorption of 6,000 personnel since 2023.

stories.t: Petrobras shifts crude to Japan and eyes fuel pricing change
stories.src: CPG Click Oil and Gas · EnergyNow
stories.b: Petrobras sent about 950,000 barrels of pre-salt crude from the Libra field to Idemitsu in Japan. This is the first time the firm shipped this oil to Japan because a crisis near Hormuz cut supplies from the Middle East. Meanwhile, oil stays below $90, and director Laureano suggests a permanent shift in the fuel pricing policy. The company also made a new oil discovery off the coast of Amapa.
stories.i: Petrobras delivered approximately 950,000 barrels of pre-salt crude from the Libra field to Idemitsu in Japan. Middle Eastern supply disruptions driven by the Hormuz crisis facilitated this maiden shipment. Director Laureano suggested a permanent shift in fuel pricing policy as oil prices remain below $90.
stories.a: Petrobras completed its inaugural crude delivery to Japan, dispatching approximately 950,000 barrels from the Libra field to Idemitsu amid supply compression originating from the Hormuz crisis. Director Laureano indicated a structural pivot in fuel pricing policy while global crude benchmarks remain sub-$90. Concurrently, exploration drilling confirmed a fresh hydrocarbon discovery offshore Amapa.

politics.b: Petrobras is owned partly by the state, and its big plans link directly to public rules and hiring choices. The firm decided against any new public hiring process after taking on 6,000 workers since 2023. At the same time, it is shifting funds into massive investments through 2031.
politics.i: State-controlled Petrobras balances heavy capital expenditure targets with administrative restraint. Management affirmed no new public hiring process following the integration of 6,000 personnel since 2023. The firm advances its $122 billion strategic plan through 2031.
politics.a: State ownership intertwines Petrobras's capital deployment with public sector employment dynamics. Leadership maintains a freeze on public hiring processes despite expanding the corporate execution portfolio to $113 billion and total outlays to $122 billion through 2031.

timeline: Petrobras announces an extraordinary dividend of R$15.60 billion.
Petrobras ships pre-salt crude from the Libra field to Japan for the first time.
Petrobras confirms no new public hiring process is planned under its $122 billion plan.
Director Laureano suggests a permanent change in fuel pricing policy.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Aramco awards offshore deals amid infrastructure attacks

stories.t: Saipem secures offshore contracts from Saudi Aramco
stories.src: Oil & Gas Middle East · MEED · Offshore Magazine
stories.b: Saipem won two major offshore deals from Saudi Aramco. Saudi Aramco is a massive state-owned oil company. Saipem is an engineering contractor that builds energy infrastructure. These new contracts cover engineering, procurement, construction, and installation work across multiple fields. Saipem will execute the projects offshore Saudi Arabia.
stories.i: Saipem secured two offshore contracts from Saudi Aramco. The deals involve engineering, procurement, construction, and installation work across multiple offshore fields. Saudi Aramco awarded these tenders to expand development capacity. Saipem will deploy marine assets to execute the scope.
stories.a: Saipem secured two offshore engineering, procurement, construction, and installation contracts from Saudi Aramco across multiple fields. The awards expand local offshore hydrocarbon processing capacity despite regional security disruptions. Saipem will mobilize regional fabrication yards and offshore spreads to fulfill the multi-field scope.

stories.t: Attacks damage Saudi Aramco facilities and disrupt pipeline flows
stories.b: Strikes hit Saudi Aramco headquarters and caused extensive damage. A separate strike wounded 11 people in Riyadh's financial hub during the third attack within three weeks. These incidents cut Saudi oil output and East-West pipeline flow according to the state news agency. Saudi Aramco also sought to reroute crude away from the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.i: Houthi attacks caused extensive damage to Saudi Aramco headquarters and wounded 11 people in Riyadh's financial hub. The state news agency confirmed that these strikes reduced Saudi oil output and interrupted East-West pipeline flows. Saudi Aramco subsequently attempted to reroute crude shipments away from the Strait of Hormuz to maintain export channels.
stories.a: Houthi strikes targeted Saudi Aramco headquarters and Riyadh's financial hub, injuring 11 individuals in the third such attack in three weeks. State media reports confirmed that the physical damage curtailed domestic oil output and restricted East-West pipeline throughput. Saudi Aramco initiated operational countermeasures to reroute crude transport away from the Strait of Hormuz.

politics.b: Saudi Arabia manages state oil production through Saudi Aramco while facing regional security threats. Officials navigate geopolitical tensions affecting OPEC production policy and shipping routes. State agencies report on infrastructure repairs and operational adjustments following recent attacks.
politics.i: State policy centers on maintaining production stability at Saudi Aramco while mitigating regional security threats from Houthi strikes. Policymakers coordinate through OPEC to manage supply agreements despite disruptions to pipeline flows and export bottlenecks. Officials balance domestic infrastructure recovery with international supply commitments.
politics.a: State governance intertwines directly with Saudi Aramco's operational security and OPEC quota compliance amidst active regional hostilities. Policymakers manage physical asset recovery alongside export logistics adjustments following strikes on domestic infrastructure. Strategic planning focuses on securing alternative transit corridors to bypass vulnerable chokepoints.

timeline: Houthi strikes wound 11 people in Riyadh's financial hub.
Attacks damage Saudi Aramco headquarters and reduce oil output and pipeline flow.
Saudi Aramco seeks to reroute crude away from the Strait of Hormuz.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Central bank steps up dollar limits and reserves shift

stories.t: CBN Raises Weekly Dollar Limit
stories.b: The Central Bank of Nigeria is the main group that manages the country's money. It has raised the weekly dollar limit for bureau de change operators to $1m. Bureau de change operators are licensed shops that trade foreign currencies. This change aims to ease pressure on the naira, which is the national currency. The limit was adjusted to help calm the local currency value.
stories.i: The Central Bank of Nigeria lifted the weekly dollar limit for bureau de change operators to $1m. This policy change attempts to relieve downward pressure on the naira. Trading desks adjusted positions following the announcement. Foreign exchange availability remains a central focus for market participants.
stories.a: The Central Bank of Nigeria expanded the weekly dollar allocation limit for bureau de change operators to $1m to compress parallel market spreads. This intervention attempts to alleviate structural liquidity bottlenecks weighing on the naira. Market participants are monitoring whether increased retail-tier supply alters interbank transmission dynamics. The policy relies on sufficient underlying foreign exchange inflows to prevent reserve depletion.

stories.t: Reserves Shift as Interbank Turnover Surges
stories.b: Foreign exchange reserves dropped by $108m, pushing the naira to N1,455 per dollar. Reserves are the country's savings of foreign money held to back its own currency. Interbank turnover surged by 328% to reach $703m later on. Interbank turnover measures the volume of trading between commercial banks. The naira subsequently rebounded following the jump in trading volume.
stories.i: Foreign exchange reserves fell by $108m, initially driving the naira down to N1,455 per dollar. Interbank foreign exchange turnover subsequently surged by 328% to $703m. This sharp rise in trading activity triggered a rebound in the naira. Central bank officials stated that reserve drops will not weaken the local currency over the long term.
stories.a: Foreign exchange reserves contracted by $108m, sending the naira down to N1,455 per dollar before interbank turnover expanded by 328% to $703m. This liquidity surge facilitated a naira rebound despite ongoing reserve erosion. Central bank commentary maintains that recent reserve fluctuations will not structurally weaken the currency. Analysts are tracking whether the newly forged partnership between the Central Bank of Nigeria and NNPC can sustain higher dollar inflows.

stories.t: Equities Index Drops in Mid-Week Selloff
stories.b: The main stock market index fell by 0.69% during a mid-week selloff. An index tracks the overall performance of a group of shares. This drop wiped out N1.10trn from the total value of listed companies. Shares are units of ownership in a business. Trading activity reflected broad declines across the stock exchange.
stories.i: The main stock exchange index declined by 0.69% during a mid-week selloff. This downward move erased N1.10trn in market capitalization. Investors offloaded equities across multiple sectors. Selling pressure dominated the trading session on the exchange.
stories.a: The primary equities benchmark index fell by 0.69%, resulting in a market capitalization loss of N1.10trn during the mid-week session. Broad-based selling pressure drove valuations lower across listed equities. This correction reflects diminished risk appetite among domestic institutional investors. Portfolio rebalancing remains the primary driver behind the persistent downward momentum.

politics.b: The Kogi State Government announced a 7 billion naira health upgrade. The same state government also commended a federal payment for campaign signage. Meanwhile, watchdogs were asked to probe a political member over cash distribution.
politics.i: The Kogi State Government announced a 7 billion naira health sector upgrade. Anti-corruption bodies faced calls to investigate a Zamfara ruling party member regarding cash distribution for mobilization. The Kogi State Government separately commended a federal campaign signage payment.
politics.a: The Kogi State Government initiated a 7 billion naira health infrastructure upgrade alongside acknowledging a campaign signage payment. Concurrently, civil society actors petitioned anti-corruption agencies to investigate a Zamfara ruling party official over alleged cash mobilization distributions ahead of future elections. These developments intersect with localized administrative expenditures and regulatory enforcement threats.

timeline: Kogi State Government commended a federal campaign payment and threatened enforcement.
Anti-corruption agencies received petitions to probe a Zamfara party member over cash distribution.
Central bank raised the weekly dollar limit for bureau de change operators to $1m.
Kogi State Government announced a 7 billion naira health upgrade.

stories.t: Australian Dollar Gains Strength From Data Centre Boom
stories.b: The Australian dollar gets a boost from a boom in data centres. A data centre is a large building full of computers that store and process digital information. This rise helps the local currency find solid support in the market. The kiwi, which is the nickname for the New Zealand dollar, moves away from a low point not seen in 17 years.
stories.i: The Australian dollar gains support from a surge in data centre construction and demand. This local currency strength contrasts with the kiwi edging away from a 17-year low.
stories.a: The Australian dollar derives fundamental backing from regional data centre infrastructure expansion. Concurrently, the New Zealand currency drifts away from a trough last tested 17 years prior.

stories.t: Arrow Minerals and Sunrise Energy Metals Post Share Price Gains
stories.b: Shares in Arrow Minerals go up by 11.8%. Arrow Minerals trades under the stock code ASX:AMD. Shares in Sunrise Energy Metals go up by 10.4% under the code ASX:SRL. Sunrise Energy Metals discusses a Nasdaq redomicile plan.
stories.i: Arrow Minerals shares rise by 11.8% under the ticker ASX:AMD. Sunrise Energy Metals shares advance 10.4% under ASX:SRL following discussion of a Nasdaq redomicile plan.
stories.a: Arrow Minerals equities rally 11.8% on the ASX. Sunrise Energy Metals securities appreciate 10.4% alongside disclosures regarding a Nasdaq redomicile plan.

politics.b: No government policies or political updates appear in the market reports today.
politics.i: No political developments or regulatory policy announcements feature in the current market trading sessions.
politics.a: No macroeconomic policy shifts or legislative announcements are registered across the source material.
